title: Refold an opened laminated pocket street map along its seven-panel accordion creases into its packet, cover outside
instruction: Fold this street map back up into its pocket-size packet, cover on the outside, and leave it lying flat on the table.
context: Refolding a map along its own creases is a chore most adults have done, and one people famously get wrong. This laminated city map is accordion folded: six creases alternate valley and mountain, and the springy laminate keeps every crease half open, so the opened map lies as a zigzag. The map has to be gathered from both ends at once, with each crease closing the way it was made. Pushed in carelessly at table height, the map bows up off the table and only some creases close.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the table. Map: Michelin Streetwise Chicago laminated city map (ISBN 9782067259973), 21.6 x 71.1 cm (8.5 x 28 in) open, 10.2 x 21.6 cm (4 x 8.5 in) folded, 68 g, printed paper laminated in plastic film, accordion folded into seven 10.16 x 21.6 cm panels by six creases running along x. Panel 1 (the cover panel, cover printed red on its underside) is at the robot's right (-y) end; crease 1 is a valley, then they alternate (valley, mountain, valley, mountain, valley, mountain). The map lies open on the table with every crease sprung back to about 60 degrees (each panel about 30 degrees from level): valley creases 1, 3, 5 on the table at y = -27.2, -9.4, 8.3; mountain creases 2, 4, 6 are ridges 5.1 cm up at y = -18.3, -0.6, 17.2. The cover panel's free edge is 5.1 cm up at y = -36.1, and the far panel's free edge lies on the table at y = 26.1. The map's long centre line runs along x = 27 (panels span x = 16.2 to 37.8). Distractors (NVIDIA SimReady, loose): reading glasses (accessory_eyeglasses_a01, 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g) at (53, 14), turned 109 degrees; empty paper coffee cup (dishware_cup_paper_a01, 8 cm across, 11 cm tall, 10 g) at (50, -20). Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read at the end from the map (real trial: the packet's edge photographed from the side shows each crease's direction, a ruler gives its height, the video shows the grippers). A crease counts as closed when its two panels are within 15 degrees of face to face (folded 165 degrees or more) the way it was made, and as reversed when it is bent 90 degrees or more the wrong way. 1.0: all six creases closed the way they were made (which puts the cover panel outside, cover face out), every panel within 15 degrees of level and every panel corner within 3 cm of the table top (the packet lying flat), every fingertip point of both grippers (each finger's tip and 3 cm up it) at least 4 cm from every panel, and every panel still (under 2 cm/s and 0.2 rad/s), all held for 1 s. 0.5: at the end, all six creases closed the way they were made and both grippers 4 cm clear, short of full credit (for example the packet left standing on its edge). 0.25: at the end, at least three creases closed the way they were made, none reversed, and both grippers 4 cm clear. 0: anything else, including the opened starting map and a gripper within 4 cm of the map. A map that goes over the table's edge (any panel corner more than 3 cm below the table top) scores 0 for the whole trial.
reset_notes: Open the map on its marks with the cover panel at the right end, cover side down. Set each ridge (creases 2, 4, 6) to 5.1 +-0.5 cm high with a ruler, valleys on the table, and the end panels' free edges at their tape marks; about 1 minute. Nothing is consumed; replace the map if a crease starts to split or a new crease forms.
fidelity: Full size: 21.6 x 71.1 cm, seven 10.2 cm panels, 68 g. Panels are rigid 1.5 mm plates (real laminate about 0.5 mm) on six hinges, with no bending between creases. Self-collision is off: a closed stack is held by joint stops. Crease spring-back is code: 0.03 N m/rad toward a 60 degree set (our estimate), and a crease folded past 160 degrees stays shut. Map-on-table friction is 0.35. The map is a custom mesh; the glasses and cup are SimReady props.
